targets.name: Jezero crater: Octavia E. Butler Landing (Perseverance)
targets.outcome_note: NASA: Perseverance landed in Jezero crater on Feb. 18, 2021, and Jezero was chosen as the landing site.
targets.center_note: Secondary source: Wikipedia 'Octavia E. Butler Landing' (rounded to 18.44 N, 77.45 E); the 4-decimal value 18.4447, 77.4508 is not confirmed by NASA/JPL.

targets.name: Gale crater: Bradbury Landing (Curiosity)
targets.outcome_note: NASA: Curiosity landed on Mars on Aug. 6, 2012 and has been exploring Gale Crater since 2012.
targets.center_note: Secondary source: Wikipedia 'Bradbury Landing' coordinate template (-4.5895, 137.4417); the NASA MSL page read gives no coordinates.

targets.name: InSight landing site, Elysium Planitia
targets.outcome_note: NASA: InSight landed on Nov. 26, 2018 at 11:52:59 a.m. PT on Elysium Planitia.
targets.center_note: Secondary source: Golombek et al. 2020 via search snippet (paper not opened, publisher HTTP 403); the NASA page gives only the 135.9 E pre-landing target.

targets.name: Gusev crater, Spirit landing site (Columbia Memorial Station)
targets.outcome_note: NASA: 'The entire rover package hit the Martian surface at 20:35 PST Jan. 3, 2004' at Gusev crater.
targets.center_note: Primary: NASA science page quotes the landing coordinates directly.

targets.name: Utopia Planitia, Zhurong landing site (Tianwen-1)
targets.outcome_note: Zhurong landed on Utopia Planitia in May 2021 and operated on the surface (Ding et al. 2022, read via snippet).
targets.center_note: Secondary source: two peer-reviewed papers read only via search snippets (Li et al. 2022; Ding et al. 2022), not opened; Wikipedia agrees.

targets.name: Oxia Planum, ExoMars Rosalind Franklin landing site (favoured ellipse)
targets.outcome_note: Planned, not flown: ESA-affiliated EPSC 2026 abstract (Sefton-Nash et al.) says the rover is 'on schedule for launch in the latter part of 2028 and to land at Oxia Planum in 2030'.
targets.center_note: Secondary source: Wikipedia mirror, favoured landing ellipse (not the plain centre); no ESA primary coordinate found.

targets.name: Apollo 17 landing site, Taurus-Littrow (control site)
targets.outcome_note: Apollo 17 landed in the Moon's Taurus-Littrow Valley in December 1972 (NASA: launch Dec. 7, 1972; splashdown Dec. 19, 1972).

targets.name: Intuitive Machines IM-1 Odysseus landing site, Malapert A area
targets.outcome_note: Odysseus came to rest on its side in Feb 2024: Intuitive Machines CEO Steve Altemus said at the Feb 23, 2024 briefing, 'we're tipped over' (NBC report of the briefing).
targets.center_note: Primary: NASA LRO release gives the resting coordinates. The tip-over statement is the company's, reported by news (NASA's release does not mention it).

targets.name: Intuitive Machines IM-2 Athena landing site, Mons Mouton area
targets.outcome_note: Athena 'hit the surface faster than intended and ended up on its side within a 20-meter diameter crater' (LROC, Mark Robinson, 10 Mar 2025).
targets.center_note: Primary: intended site from LROC. The LROC page gives no touchdown point; the 6 km disk covers it. Touchdown offset not measured here.
